section_summary.extract_value: This section presents central analyses results from a single study examining within-persons and between-persons interactions between self-compassion and frequency of interactions with body-focused others in predicting intuitive eating, body appreciation, body image concerns, and negative affect. The analyses reveal that on days with lower self-compassion, higher frequency of body-focused interactions is associated with less intuitive eating, lower body appreciation, more body image concerns, and more negative affect; these relationships reverse or disappear on days with higher self-compassion. At the between-persons level, higher mean frequency of body-focused interactions is negatively related to intuitive eating and body appreciation among individuals with low and average self-compassion levels, but unrelated among those with high self-compassion.
